AUSTIN, Texas, Oct 24 : Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli will start on pole position for a US Grand Prix that could make him Formula One's youngest world champion if results go his way on Sunday. Red Bull's Max Verstappen joined the 20-year-old Italian on the front row after Saturday's qualifying at Austin's Circuit of the Americas with teammate Isack Hadjar qualifying third and Ferrari's Charles Leclerc completing the second row. Antonelli has a 102-point lead in the championship over closest rival and teammate George Russell, who qualified only sixth, with 125 points still to be won after Sunday. To take the title, the Italian will need to win with Russell and Ferrari's seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton finishing no higher than ninth or fifth respectively.

Hamilton qualified fifth after setting the fastest time in final practice. The pole was Antonelli's first since Belgium in July and he found the speed just when he needed it after Ferrari had dominated practice. "It feels good to be back," he said over the team radio after a gusty session. "We got pole, so we will try to win tomorrow," he added in comments to the crowd after stepping out of the car. "Max has been very quick and Isack did an incredible job, so it won't be easy. We will try to get a good start and hopefully we lead into Turn One, then set the pace, even though it will be very tight."

Commentary: Trump should reject Putin’s plan for a great powers summit

There’s little prospect of true negotiation on the Ukraine war until after the winter, says Marc Champion for Bloomberg Opinion.

Visitors stand in front of an artwork depicting US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping at an exhibition, which is called "Yalta 2.0" and opened to make a reference to the 1945 Yalta Conference, at an art gallery in Livadia park in Yalta, Crimea, Feb 8, 2025. FAST

LONDON: The mere prospect of Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump meeting for a great-powers summit while at the Asia Pacific Economic Community’s annual gathering next month is causing concern among America’s traditional allies, not to mention Ukraine. Rightly so. One reason for caution is the very fact that Putin has been pressing for this for some time, most recently in his Oct 9 phone call with the US president. The Kremlin says preparations are underway, but Trump should ask why it is that Moscow is so interested before he commits to attending. One attraction is that the plan would exclude Ukraine and Europe, the two objects of Russian aggression and therefore the ones most likely to get in the way of the wider deal Putin is looking for. Indeed, when US Special Envoy for Peace Missions Steve Witkoff this week delivered an updated ceasefire proposal he worked out with Ukrainian and Europeans leaders in Oslo, the response from Kremlin point-man Yuri Ushakov was dismissive. It lacked substance, he said.

The charade around peace efforts will continue for a while yet; Ushakov said the Russians might be interested in resuming lower-level talks next month, before the possible three-way summit at APEC’s Nov 18 to 19 meeting in Southern China. But there’s little prospect of a true negotiation until after the winter. Putin believes he has a big enough advantage in the long-range air war that he will emerge next spring with a rump Ukraine that has either capitulated or lies in ruins. He would count either as a win.

WHAT TRUMP AND PUTIN CAN GAIN Trump doesn’t appear to care about this, as he’s more interested in the potential commercial benefits of a US-Russia reset. So this week he ignored all evidence of daily Russian attacks on civilian targets to say that Russia was “fine” on Ukraine and “hasn’t been doing much”. Witkoff, meeting Putin on Wednesday (Oct 21), even praised Russia’s president as “a humanitarian”. Two days earlier, one of Putin’s Shahed-style loitering munitions – which circle until locked onto something to strike – had killed six people in a park in Ukraine’s Kharkiv region. The victims included a one-year-old girl in a stroller, together with her mother and two more children; 14 others, including other children, were wounded. Trump no doubt bets he can blame the war’s continuation on Europe and Zelenskyy, and that news of Russian oil tankers steaming toward the US with diesel (to lower prices at the pump) will help him politically ahead of the midterms on Nov 3. Sadly, some American voters may agree, while the gravitas and razzmatazz that a great-powers summit brings could help, too.  For Putin, the stakes are higher. From the day his armies invaded in 2022, he has made clear that his goal is not just to seize territory, but to change the entire security architecture of Europe in a way that allows Russia to restore influence across the continent and reestablish itself as a great power. A three-way meeting in China would plant a decisive flag in that quest and is made yet more attractive by the fact that Xi is a close ally. It would be two against one, on Xi’s home turf. I would happily support giving Putin that win if it would unlock the door to compromise on Ukraine and other points of global tension. But that isn’t how it would work. Putin does not want recognition of Russia as a great power just for reasons of status. He seeks the right to do what great powers do: establish dominance over the nations around them.

Related:

Commentary: This is an era of Davids, not Goliaths

Commentary: Russia’s new jet‑powered drones mark latest evolution in air war above Ukraine

A SECOND YALTA CONFERENCE Hence the excitement in Russia’s state-controlled media over the possibility that Shenzhen could serve as a second Yalta conference. At the first, in 1945, Winston Churchill, Franklin D Roosevelt and Joseph Stalin not only created a framework for the United Nations but also agreed to enable the self-determination – via free democratic elections – of the countries they occupied. Stalin, of course, reneged, continuing the de-facto Soviet occupation of what later would become the Warsaw Pact. To his credit, Trump seems to be pushing discussion of the potential China summit’s agenda toward nuclear arms control, not Ukraine or spheres of influence. This is an important area for diplomacy. It’s also one in which US and Russian interests coincide against China’s. Xi is building his country’s nuclear arsenal quickly, but it remains far from parity, which would likely make any arms-control deal that would suit Moscow and Washington unattractive to Beijing. How would it then catch up? That’s one reason the meeting might not happen, which might be for the best given the checkered record that great-power summits enjoy. They tend to depend heavily on both the balance of power on the day and the relative personal strengths and weaknesses of the leaders involved. Munich, in 1938, needs no further comment. Yalta was shaped by the fact that three wartime allies at the table still had millions of troops on the ground, while Roosevelt was sick with heart disease and a brain tumour (he died soon afterward) and together with Churchill overly trusting of Stalin, who played them. A divided Europe and the Cold War followed. John F Kennedy’s 1961 summit with Nikita Khrushchev was a diplomatic car crash that would have been better skipped. Khrushchev came away thinking Kennedy weak, unprepared and undisciplined. The Berlin airlift and Cuban missile crisis followed, as the Soviet leader tried to press an advantage he thought he had.

Related:

Commentary: Trump’s Russian diesel U-turn comes at bad time for Ukraine

Commentary: America is risking its biggest asset

ASSESSING TRUMP’S PROSPECTS So how to assess Trump’s prospects in Shenzhen, should the summit materialise? The first thing to say is that the US president has a track record in high-profile summitry that is not encouraging. He has repeatedly given leverage away for nothing in his dealings with Putin, proving himself far too trusting of a career intelligence handler. His red carpet meetings with the Russian leader in Anchorage last year, and with North Korea’s Kim Jong Un in 2018, both suffered from poor preparation akin to Kennedy’s. Trump is notorious for not engaging with detail and there would be just weeks for sherpas to prepare. Second, the wider circumstances would not be propitious for any American leader. The US is engaged in a draining war that has no obvious path to success in Iran, a country supported by both China and Russia. This gives them leverage in any negotiation, whereas Trump already gave up much of his in Ukraine by withdrawing most US support. America’s strong alliances in Europe and Asia – formerly a major advantage over both Beijing and Moscow – are weakening, undermined primarily by US actions. Those ties would be further damaged by any agreement made over their heads in China, especially if it were to trade their geopolitical loss for US commercial gain, as Trump is wont to do. Even if there were no attempt at a second Yalta and a three-way meeting took place in Shenzhen for purely symbolic value, it could still have costs in the form of distraction. For amid all the noise, the world would be led to believe something was being done to end Russia’s invasion of Ukraine and its potential for escalation in Europe, when it wasn’t. That works only for Putin.

Source: Bloomberg/el

MADRID, Oct 24 : Julian Alvarez gave Atletico Madrid supporters a winning goal and an apology on Saturday, sealing a 1-0 victory over Deportivo La Coruna before seeking forgiveness for declaring his desire to play for Barcelona. The Argentine striker scored for the second successive match as Atletico moved within two points of LaLiga leaders Barca, then addressed the comments that had soured his relationship with fans at the Metropolitano. "I'd like to apologise to our fans for what I said at the World Cup; it was a mistake in terms of how I said it and the timing," Alvarez told Spanish broadcaster Movistar Plus. "I understand why the fans are angry. If I were a fan, I'd be angry too. Especially given how they've supported me since I arrived."

Regularly booed at home this season, Alvarez received a standing ovation from some supporters after Saturday's goal. "I hope that with hard work and humility I can turn this situation around," he said. "I've been feeling better in recent matches – both physically and on the ball. I want to help the team and give my best." Second-placed Atletico have 25 points. Real Madrid, third with 21, visit Barcelona at Camp Nou on Sunday for the season's first Clasico.

ABU DHABI, Oct 24 : Australian Alexander Volkanovski retained his UFC featherweight title with a second-round technical knockout of Movsar Evloev at UFC 333 on Saturday, ending the Russian's unbeaten 20-fight professional run and keeping a promise to his wife. A thunderous combination sent Evloev backing up against the cage and Volkanovski followed him to the canvas before landing a series of unanswered blows that caused referee Marc Goddard to call off the fight with six seconds remaining in the frame.  "It feels good to get a finish - I actually promised the missus, it was our wedding anniversary on Wednesday, I promised her a quick one so she wasn't stressing on the sideline, so there you go," he said grinning at his post-fight interview.  The 38-year-old twice champion got through the first round without suffering too much damage and began to make his presence felt with precise striking in the second round, briefly sending Evloev to the canvas with a glancing blow to his temple.

Evloev, 32, did his best to leverage his superior grappling but had no answer to Volkanovski's shrewd fighting style, which has been honed in a string of performances in title fights that have led pundits to consider him the best-ever featherweight.  "I feel the love ... thank you so much. I really do appreciate it, I feel it from everyone, from the UFC staff, the fighters, every fan. The love that I get is just incredible, and I'm so thankful for it, so thank you all," he said.  In the co-main event at The Etihad Arena on Yas Island, Russia's Petr Yan retained his bantamweight crown with a unanimous decision over Georgian Merab Dvalishvili in a battle fought at a frenetic pace from the first bell.  The 33-year-old Yan, who took the belt from Dvalishvili by unanimous decision in December 2025, withstood a stream of takedown attempts and his piston-like punches left his opponent sporting several red welts on his face at the end of the fight. Facing Yan for the third time in his UFC career, Dvalishvili showed heart and courage, bouncing back repeatedly after shots to the body and head, but Yan kept his cool to pick him off, winning 48-47 on the scorecards of all three judges.

BEIJING: The Chinese commerce ministry urged the United States on Saturday (Oct 24) to stop expanding restrictions on American investments in China , saying a proposed rule on sensitive technologies would disrupt trade ties. The US Treasury Department issued proposals on Thursday to update its outbound-investment security programme , adding biotechnology to restricted sectors and expanding coverage of high-performance computing and hypersonic systems. Beijing's commerce ministry said in a statement that the proposal "discriminatorily" widened China -related investment restrictions and intensified curbs. It firmly opposed the US proposal and reserved the right to take unspecified countermeasures, it added. Beijing also said the proposal would damage bilateral economic ties and ran counter to the consensus reached by the countries' presidents, who have met twice in the past six months. The US Treasury has said the measures, which do not only cover China , are intended to stop US capital from supporting foreign adversaries' development of dual-use strategic technologies that could threaten US national security. The US programme had already restricted certain US investments involving China in semiconductors, quantum technologies and artificial intelligence.

LONDON, Oct 24 : Tottenham Hotspur's 2-0 win at London rivals Chelsea – only their second at Stamford Bridge since Margaret Thatcher was Britain’s prime minister – was greeted by their coach, players and fans as a turning point in their season. Roberto De Zerbi's men were bottom of the Premier League before they beat fellow strugglers Coventry City 3-1 at home on Monday and Saturday’s victory propelled them to 12th place pending the rest of the weekend’s fixtures. The north Londoners had won once in their previous 41 visits to Chelsea in all competitions - a run stretching back to February 1990 when Gary Lineker scored the winning goal. Their only previous win at Chelsea during that 36-year drought was a 3-1 victory in 2018.

No wonder the away fans celebrated at the final whistle as if they had just won a trophy and the Spurs players could be heard from the Stamford Bridge press room jumping up and down in the changing room still wearing their boots. "I think we are playing well, not just today," De Zerbi told BBC Radio once the celebrations abated. "Maybe now there is another atmosphere, there is another union amongst the players. With these two wins in a row they can believe more and more in themselves," the Italian said before later telling reporters: "We have suffered enough." There was a touch of luck to the result - the match seemed to be heading to a 0-0 stalemate before Chelsea goalkeeper Mike Penders, on his full Premier League debut, punched the ball into his own net from a Matheus Fernandes corner. Spurs made sure of the win with a breakaway strike by Mathys Tel 10 minutes later. "It's very special because we have come to Chelsea so many times and not got a win," the French striker told Sky Sports. "We showed great mentality today and we need to enjoy this win." In between the goals, Chelsea playmaker Cole Palmer was sent off for the first time in his senior career when he was booked twice in nine minutes. Spurs dominated possession with 70 per cent of the ball over the match and 15 shots to Chelsea's seven. The Blues, who remain fourth in the table ahead of Sunday's matches, looked far from their fluent best and missed the focal point of top scorer Joao Pedro who was injured in training on Friday and is due to undergo tests in the coming days. "We need to be self-critical. We need to be at a better level," Chelsea coach Xabi Alonso told the BBC. "Sometimes you feel good and today, collectively and individually, we were not at our best." Asked about Palmer picking up two yellow cards in quick succession, Alonso said he wanted to see more self-control among his players, who last season racked up eight reds. "In those situations, the first yellow card can be decisive," the Spaniard said. "It’s a process of the maturity of the team and of the individual players as well."

(Writing by William SchombergEditing by Toby Davis)

Oct 24 : Burnley have parted ways with head coach Nicky Hayen after just 14 matches, the Championship club said on Saturday, following a poor start to the season. The 46-year-old Belgian's final game in charge was Saturday's 4-1 defeat at Lincoln City, a result that extended Burnley's struggles and left them 22nd in the table. Burnley have won only once in their last 12 league matches. "Burnley Football Club has dismissed head coach Nicky Hayen with immediate effect. The Board has taken the decision following a disappointing start to the Championship season," the club said in a statement. Hayen was appointed on a three-year deal in the summer, replacing Scott Parker, who left by mutual consent in April after Burnley's relegation from the Premier League was confirmed, with the club dropping into the Championship for the third time in five seasons

NAPLES, Italy, Oct 24 : Lazio climbed to the top of the Serie A table with a 2-1 home win over Parma on Saturday as AS Roma twice came from behind to secure a 3-3 draw with Napoli in a pulsating Serie A clash in Naples. Lazio have 22 points from their eight matches this season and are three points clear of champions Inter Milan, who have played a game fewer and host Fiorentina on Sunday. Lazio opened the scoring in the 50th minute as Kenneth Taylor netted his first goal of the season, before Parma's Diego Carlos put the ball into his own net trying to cut out a cross. The visitors scored a late consolation through Simone Lontani.

Third-placed Roma trailed 2-0 and then 3-2 late on, so will be pleased with a point in Naples as they preserved their 15-game unbeaten run in Serie A that dates back to April. Frank Anguissa’s spectacular overhead kick gave Napoli the lead and Scott McTominay doubled the advantage. At that stage they were cruising, but two goals in four minutes from Matias Soule and Leonardo Balerdi drew Roma level. When McTominay added his second in the closing stages the momentum swung back in Napoli’s favour, but Balerdi headed an equaliser for Roma with a minute remaining.    "We maintained roles, positions and our way of playing," Roma coach Gian Piero Gasperini told DAZN. "The goals were of quality. We are fine (with the result), with high morale. "Balerdi knows football, has extraordinary energy and has been a great (loan) signing for us." DOUVIKAS DOUBLE Two second-half goals from Anastasios Douvikas took Como to a 2-0 victory against Sassuolo as the Greek striker continued his red-hot form. He has scored five goals in his last four games in all competitions and provided two clinical finishes in the box as Como climbed to fourth place with 17 points from their eight games. Sassuolo are in 14th. "He (Douvikas) is growing in a way that could make him a very, very important centre-forward," Como coach Cesc Fabregas said. "In the last three years he has been one of those signings that has given a lot of satisfaction." Bologna were 2-0 winners at Cagliari as they claimed their second victory of the season.  Defender Nicolo Casale scored his first goal in almost four years to give Bologna the lead before Federico Bernardeschi doubled the advantage for the visitors. "It was a very difficult game on a tough pitch," Bernardeschi said. "These games are won with character. Cagliari made us suffer, but in the second half we reacted well."
